items.title: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Brandon Aiyuk will not be elevated from the practice squad for Washington’s Week 12 game against the Cardinals.
items.text: No surprise or shame there — Aiyuk literally just signed on Wednesday. We are curious to see if he’ll be able to get active for Week 13, when the Commanders have a tasty matchup against the Jeffrey Simmons-less Titans. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Brock Bowers (ankle) was not seen practicing on Friday.
items.text: Bowers was limited on Wednesday and Thursday. ESPN’s Ryan McFadden noted yesterday that Bowers’ right ankle was “heavily wrapped up” yesterday, which wasn’t the case on Wednesday. Hopefully, today’s absence during the portion of practice open to the media is only a precautionary, rest-related move. We should know more when the official injury report drops later. Stay tuned. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: ESPN’s Todd Archer reports Jake Ferguson has partial tears in his MCL and PCL.
items.text: That explains why Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Ferguson would likely be out “multiple weeks” after injuring his knee in Week 9 against the Colts. We haven’t had an official update in a while, but the Cowboys are on bye in Week 14. Perhaps a Week 15 return is possible. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: Bears announced Colston Loveland (knee) is “week to week.”
items.text: This was the same status they gave Caleb Williams ahead of him missing Weeks 3-5 with his hamstring injury, so fantasy managers should expect a multi-week absence even if this sprain isn’t something that will send him to injured reserve. Earlier reporting has focused on the idea that he could return before the end of the regular season. The Bears have a Friday game in Week 16 so if Loveland isn’t back for Week 15, it will be difficult to turn him around for that one. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Cole Holcomb (heel) will not play in the Steelers’ Week 12 game against the Broncos.
items.text: Holcomb was the only player listed as questionable entering the weekend, but the team has opted to sit him for this one after he suffered a heel injury in the previous week’s loss to the Eagles. In addition to Holcomb, the Steelers also declared WR Kaden Weten, QB Drew Allar, CB Sean Murphy-Bunting, RB Eli Heidenreich, LB Alex Highsmith, and DT Gabe Rubio inactive for this week. Will Howard will serve as the backup for starting QB Mason Rudolph. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Broncos declared QB Sam Ehlinger, WR Lil’Jordan Humphrey S Taylor Rapp, OL Gavin Ortega, OL Kage Casey, and TE Dallen Bentley inactive for Week 12 against the Steelers.
items.text: The Broncos will be operating at close to full strength against the Steelers in a game that could feature some inclement weather and low temperatures. Rookie running back Jonah Coleman could be in line for a busy day, with J.K. Dobbins suspended by the team for this week. Coleman rushed 24 times for 111 yards and three touchdowns in last week’s win over the Raiders. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will not play in Atlanta’s Week 12 game against the Vikings.
items.text: Branch has now been sidelined each of the last four weeks, missing Week 9 and 10 before their Week 11 bye, and did not practice at any point this week. If only there were some sort of “injured reserve” list for players who weren’t close to playing. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Jahan Dotson (hamstring) won’t play in Atlanta’s Week 12 game against the Vikings.
items.text: Olmaide Zachcheaus will be Atlanta’s No. 2 receiver behind Drake London, and after that it turns to Chris Blair and Beaux Collins with Zachariah Branch also hurt. This will likely be a situation that forces the Falcons to condense the target tree and throw at their main three of Drake London, Bijan Robinson, and Kyle Pitts. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Denzel Boston (quad) is questionable for the Browns’ Week 12 game against the Raiders.
items.text: According to Cabot, Boston was a DNP all week but still managed to draw the questionable tag. Given his week’s worth of DNPs, it’s hard to imagine the rookie suiting up on Sunday night, but it sounds like the Browns will give him some additional time to try and heal up before ruling him out. Fantasy managers planning to hold out until a decision is made would be wise to stash Jerry Jeudy or another player from Sunday or Monday night’s games as a pivot off Boston in the event he is ruled out. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said he “wouldn’t anticipate” Romeo Doubs (shoulder) being ready for action yet.
items.text: Doubs was limited in each of the first two practices this week, and we’re guessing he won’t do better than that today based on this statement. Most players on IR will get a questionable tag on their chances to return regardless of the surrounding data, but we’d be surprised if Doubs didn’t sit this week based on what his coach said. - Rivers McCown
